html:
A fortress on the European shore of the Bosporus, built in about four months in 1452 by Mehmed II to cut Constantinople off from the Black Sea.

It stands at the narrowest point of the strait, facing Anadoluhisarı, the fort his great grandfather Bayezid I had built on the Asian side during his blockade. Thousands of workers built its towers and walls, and Mehmed's chief officers each had to finish one part. The Turks called it Boğazkesen, which means both "strait cutter" and "throat cutter".

Its cannon stopped any ship that would not pay. In November 1452 a Venetian ship tried to run past and was sunk, and its captain was executed. The city's grain from the Black Sea was now cut off, a clear sign that the final siege was coming. The fortress is well preserved and is now a museum in Istanbul.
sum: A fortress on the European shore of the Bosporus, built in about four months in 1452 by Mehmed II to cut Constantinople off from the Black Sea.
